sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 277. Whoever, knowing any drug or medical preparation to have been adulterated in such a manner as to lessen its efficacy, to change its operation, or to render it noxious, sells the same, or offers or exposes it for sale, or issues it from any dispensary for medicinal purposes as unadulterated, or causes it to be used for medicinal purposes by any person not knowing of the adulteration, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 277 constitutes a key component of Chapter XV (Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing sale of adulterated drugs. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of sale of adulterated drugs under Section 277 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 277.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 277 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 277 vs General Attempt: Section 277 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XV; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 277 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 277 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals.

Rule: Under BNS s. 277, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 277.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 277 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
